title: Informed Consent for LEP Patients
summary: Learn how to conduct informed consent with patients who have limited English proficiency, including interpreter use, teach-back, risks.
body_markdown:
###


The patient should receive the explanation, risks, benefits, alternatives, questions, and decision process through language support they can use comfortably.


###


No. A translated form can support written communication, but informed consent also needs an understandable conversation and opportunity for questions.


###


Federal language-access rules do not prescribe one universal interpretation modality for every consent encounter. The method used should provide meaningful access and work for the patient and communication at issue.


###


Ask the patient to explain the procedure, major risks, alternatives, and next steps in their own words, with the response interpreted back to the clinician.


###


Yes. AI medical interpretation can support consent when the system supports the patient's language, communication remains clear, and the organization has a pathway to change methods when needed.
